instructions: Toast the pecans in a dry skillet over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pan often, until they smell nutty. Transfer them to a plate to cool, then chop roughly.
Slice half the red onion very thinly and soak it in a bowl of cold water while you prep the rest, which softens its bite.
In a jar, shake together the balsamic vinegar, olive oil, poppy seeds, honey, Dijon, salt and pepper until it holds together.
Hull and quarter the strawberries. Crumble the feta into rough pieces.
Put the spinach and strawberries in a large bowl. Drain the onion and add it. Pour in about half the dressing and toss, so the leaves are lightly coated and not wet through.
Add the feta and pecans, toss gently and serve right away with the rest of the dressing on the side.
For packed lunches, keep the dressing in its own jar and pack the pecans separately. The undressed salad keeps in the fridge up to 4 days, and the dressing up to 5.
method_notes: WellPlated is the lead (4.69 from 649): spinach, strawberries, red onion, feta and pecans with a balsamic poppy seed dressing, tossed with half the dressing first so the leaves aren't swimming. Love and Lemons uses a white wine vinegar and shallot dressing and makes the same point about keeping the dressing apart for make ahead; the creamier mayonnaise and yogurt dressings from Cooking Classy and Chef Savvy were not used. The pecans are toasted in a skillet rather than the oven to save time, and the amounts are cut from 6 servings to 4.
